deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page sets up the theta/Gamma machinery of the 1859 paper. This page is a working draft for two ingredients of Riemann's explicit formula for f(x) = sum_n pi(x^{1/n})/n. The first is the Li(x^beta) term attached to each factor log(1 - s/beta). The second is the integral term coming from the Gamma factor. Here Pi(s) = Gamma(s+1) and 'd log x' means dx/x.

(A) Frullani-type integrals.
(1) int_0^oo e^{-sx} dx = 1/s.
(2) int_0^oo e^{sx} e^{-alpha x} dx = 1/(alpha - s), for Re s < Re alpha.
(3) Integrating (2) in s from 0 to s [my step]: int_0^oo (e^{sx} - 1) e^{-alpha x}/x dx = -log(1 - s/alpha).
(4) Substituting x -> log x gives the multiplicative form: int_1^oo x^{alpha - s} dlog x = 1/(s - alpha), for Re(s - alpha) > 0.
(5) Integrating (4) in alpha from 0 to alpha [my step]: int_1^oo (x^alpha - 1) x^{-s}/log x dlog x = log s - log(s - alpha) = -log(1 - alpha/s). Hence -int(...) = log(1 - alpha/s). The marginal condition reads roughly 'if the real part of s - alpha is positive'.

(B) The Li term.
Riemann considers x^{-s} Li(x^alpha), where Li(x^alpha) = int_0^x x^alpha dlog x / log x. He integrates int_1^oo x^{-s} Li(x^alpha) dlog x by parts:
= [-(1/s) x^{-s} Li(x^alpha)]_{1+eps}^oo + (1/s) int_{1+eps}^oo x^{alpha-s}/log x dlog x.
Both pieces diverge logarithmically at x = 1 and must be combined. Further down the page (line 'f(1) = ...', perhaps f(beta)) is the cleaner route that Riemann actually published. Since d/dbeta Li(x^beta) = int_0^x x^beta dlog x = x^beta/beta, one has
int_1^oo x^{-s} (x^beta/beta) dlog x = (1/beta) int_1^oo x^{beta-s} dlog x = -(1/beta) * 1/(beta - s).
This equals -d/dbeta[(1/s) log(1 - s/beta)]. Integrating in beta gives (1/s) log(1 - s/beta) = -int_1^oo Li(x^beta) x^{-s} dlog x, exactly as in the 1859 paper.

(C) Gamma-function representations.
(6) Gauss's integral: psi(s) = d log Pi(s)/ds = int_0^1 [1/log(1/z) - z^s/(1-z)] dz.
(7) Integrating in s from 0, using int_0^s z^t dt = (z^s - 1)/log z [my step]: log Pi(s) = int_0^1 [s/log(1/z) - (z^s - 1)/((1-z) log z)] dz, for s > -1.
(8) Put G(z) = int_0^z dt/((1-t) log t), which is finite at 0 and behaves like -1/(1-z) near z = 1. Integrating the second term by parts on [0, 1-eps]:
log Pi(s) = -[G z^s]_0^{1-eps} (presumably with z^s - 1, so that the term G(1-eps) is included) + s int dz/log(1/z) + s int_0^{1-eps} z^s G(z) dlog z.
(9) Splitting s int dz/log(1/z) = s int z^s dz/log(1/z) + s int (1 - z^s)/log(1/z) dz, and using dz = z dlog z:
log Pi(s) = s int_0^1 z^s [G(z) -/+ z/log z] dlog z + s int_0^1 (1 - z^s)/log(1/z) dz.
The marginal notes 'log z = log(1 + (z-1)) = z - 1 ...' and 'int dz/(z-1)^2 = -1/(z-1)' check that G and z/log z have the same singularity -1/(1-z) at z = 1, so that it cancels. The last integral equals s log(1+s) by Frullani [mine].
(10) Dividing by s and differentiating, the elementary pieces cancel [my check: -int z^{s+1} dlog z + int z^s dz = 0]:
d/ds[log Pi(s)/s] = int_0^1 z^s log z G(z) dlog z.
(11) Substituting z = x^2 (G(x^2) = int_0^x t dt/((1-t^2) log t)):
= 4 int_0^1 x^{2s} log x int_0^x x dx/((1-x^2) log x) dlog x.
(12) Substituting z = 1/x in (10):
= int_1^oo x^{-s} log x int_x^oo [1/(u-1)] dlog u/log u dlog x.
The same kernel 1/(x-1) appears in the marginal 'int x^{-s} int_oo^x dlog x/((x-1) log x) dlog x'. For Pi(s/2), i.e. starting from (11), the kernel becomes 1/(x^2-1). This is exactly the term int_x^oo dx/((x^2-1) x log x) of Riemann's explicit formula, coming from the trivial zeros.

(D) Comparison with zeta.
(13) Since log zeta(s)/s = int_1^oo f(x) x^{-s} dlog x (1859 paper), one gets d/ds[log zeta(s)/s] = -int_1^oo f(x) log x x^{-s} dlog x. This is the same shape as (12), which lets the Gamma contribution to f(x) be read off.
(14) Inversion step: int_{a-bi}^{a+bi} log zeta(s)/s^2 y^s ds. This is a Perron/Mellin inversion integral, with a 1/s^2 kernel; it recovers the integrated function int_1^y f(x) dlog x. The last line, -log zeta(s)/(ss) = int_0^oo ..., is fragmentary.
errors: Line (8): as transcribed, the boundary term -(G z^s)|_0^{1-eps} omits the contribution G(1-eps) coming from the '-1' in (z^s - 1). The image suggests z^s was overwritten, possibly to (z^s - 1); if not, a term is missing. Both G(1-eps) and the other pieces diverge like 1/eps and are only meaningful in combination.

Line (9): the combined integrand must be G(z) - z/log z, since s int dz/log(1/z) = -s int z/log z dlog z. With '+' the singularities at z = 1 would add instead of cancel. Either a sign slip or a misreading of the transcription.

Line (12): the inner kernel obtained by substituting z = 1/x in (10) is 1/(x-1) * dlog x/log x, matching Riemann's own marginal formula. The transcribed x/(x-1) (or x/(x^2-1), as the image may read) matches neither the z = 1/x form nor the x = 1/u version of (11), whose kernel is 1/(x^2-1). It looks like a slip, or a mixing of the Pi(s) and Pi(s/2) versions.

The integration by parts for x^{-s} Li(x^alpha) on [1+eps, oo) produces two separately divergent terms (logarithmic singularity at x = 1). Riemann abandons it for the cleaner d/dbeta route, which is the one used in the 1859 paper.
If the line 'f(1) = ...' is read as written, it is unclear: it should be the value for parameter beta. The sign -1/(beta(beta-s)) is correct only with the minus sign visible in the image.

deep.surprise_reason: This is scratch work for the derivations in the 1859 paper: the Li(x^beta) terms, the log(1 - s/beta) Frullani step, and the Gamma-factor integral term, all in Riemann's own notation. Gauss's digamma integral and its log-Gamma corollary are classical. The reductions of d/ds(log Pi(s)/s) to iterated integrals show his route to the int dx/((x^2-1) x log x) term. That is a mildly interesting process detail of a known result, but nothing new.

In the integration-by-parts line the boundary term carries a minus sign: = (-(1/s) x^{-s} int_0^x ...)_{1+eps}^oo + (1/s) int ...
The value after 'f(1) = ... = (1/beta) int_1^oo x^{beta-s} dlog x' reads '-(1/beta) * 1/(beta - s)' (minus sign present). The label 'f(1)' may be 'f(beta)' or similar.
In the line 'int dz/(z-1)^2 = 1/(z-1) log z' the image appears to read 'int -dz/(z-1)^2 = 1/(z-1)', with 'log z' belonging to a separate expression.

In the combined integrand s int_0^1 z^s (G + z/log z) dlog z, the sign should mathematically be '-'; check the image.
The inner kernel of the last Pi-line, transcribed as x/(x-1), may read 1/(x-1) or x/(x^2-1); mathematically 1/(x-1) is required for that line.
Line '-log zeta(s)/(ss) = int_0^oo ...': the integrand is largely struck/illegible and the lower limit may be 1.
